# Rome Golf Cart Guide

> Independent comparison of golf cart tours in Rome, Italy: prices, duration, hotel pickup, private vs small-group, food, night, catacombs and cruise-port tours. Updated October 2026.

Key facts:
- Golf cart tours in Rome usually last 2.5–3 hours (express 1.5 h, full day 6–8 h) and cover 6–8 major sights from outside, with photo stops.
- Prices: shared express from about $69 per person; shared classic about $100–150 per person; private about $81–230 per person or $400–800 per cart; cruise day trips from Civitavecchia from about €790 per group.
- Most private tours include pickup at hotels in the historic center (inside the Aurelian Walls). Shared tours start from a meeting point.
- Carts usually seat 5–7. A folded wheelchair takes about two seats. Some operators give free child seats for ages 2–12 and don't accept infants under 2.
- Tours stop outside monuments; entry tickets (Colosseum, Vatican) are not included.
- Personal help choosing a tour: WhatsApp +39 393 855 2086.

## Guides
- [The best golf cart tours in Rome for 2026](https://romegolfcartguide.com/best-golf-cart-tours-rome/): The best golf cart tour in Rome overall is a private city highlights tour with hotel pickup (rated 4.9/5 on GetYourGuide). For value, the 1.5-hour Biga Tours express tour from $69 is hard to beat; for families, the VIP tour with Trevi skip-the-line, gelato and supplì (4.8/5 from 858 reviews); and for evenings, the Rome By Night private tour (4.9/5).
- [Private golf cart tours in Rome](https://romegolfcartguide.com/private-golf-cart-tour-rome/): A private golf cart tour in Rome usually lasts 2.5–3 hours and costs about $81–230 per person, or roughly $400–800 for the whole cart. Most include pickup at hotels in the historic center, and you can choose the stops.
- [Golf cart tours with hotel pickup](https://romegolfcartguide.com/golf-cart-tour-rome-hotel-pickup/): Most private golf cart tours in Rome include free pickup and drop-off at hotels in the historic center, usually inside the Aurelian Walls. Shared small-group tours normally start from a meeting point instead. Add your hotel details when you book, ideally 24 hours ahead.
- [How much does a golf cart tour in Rome cost?](https://romegolfcartguide.com/golf-cart-tour-rome-price/): Golf cart tours in Rome start at about $69 per person for a 1.5-hour shared tour. Classic 3-hour shared tours cost about $100–150 per person, private tours about $81–230 per person ($400–800 per cart), and cruise day trips from Civitavecchia start around €790 per group.
- [Night golf cart tours in Rome](https://romegolfcartguide.com/rome-night-golf-cart-tour/): Night golf cart tours in Rome usually run for about 2 hours, starting around sunset. You see the Colosseum, Trevi Fountain, Piazza Navona and other landmarks lit up, with fewer crowds and cooler temperatures. They're most popular from May to September, and private evening tours can be arranged year-round.
- [Golf cart tours with gelato and food](https://romegolfcartguide.com/rome-golf-cart-food-tour/): Several Rome golf cart tours include food: some add a gelato or espresso stop to a 3-hour sightseeing route, while others finish with a tasting of classic Roman pastas in a trattoria. Expect about $99–130 per person on a shared tour and more for private food tours.
- [Catacombs and Appian Way by golf cart](https://romegolfcartguide.com/catacombs-appian-way-golf-cart-tour/): Catacombs and Appian Way golf cart tours take about 2.5 hours from central Rome and cost from about $108 per person. They drive out along the ancient Via Appia Antica and include entry with a guided visit of about 30–35 minutes inside one of the Christian catacombs.
- [Rome by golf cart from Civitavecchia cruise port](https://romegolfcartguide.com/civitavecchia-cruise-golf-cart-tour-rome/): Golf cart shore excursions from Civitavecchia include a private transfer to Rome (about 1–1.5 hours each way), around 5 hours touring the center by golf cart, and the return to your ship on time. They're private for your group and start from about €790 per group.
- [Golf cart tours for seniors and limited mobility](https://romegolfcartguide.com/golf-cart-tour-rome-seniors/): Golf cart tours are one of the easiest ways for seniors and people with limited mobility to see Rome: the cart drives right up to the main sights and most private tours include hotel pickup. Many operators accept wheelchairs; a folded wheelchair usually takes the space of two seats, so mention it when booking.
- [Golf cart tours in Rome with kids](https://romegolfcartguide.com/golf-cart-tour-rome-with-kids/): Golf cart tours are great for families in Rome: kids enjoy the ride and nobody gets tired of walking. Some operators provide free child seats for ages 2–12 but don't accept infants under 2, while others allow babies in a pram or stroller. Private tours with hotel pickup and a gelato stop are the easiest option.
- [Golf cart, walking tour or hop-on bus?](https://romegolfcartguide.com/golf-cart-vs-walking-tour-rome/): A golf cart tour covers 6–8 major sights in about 3 hours with almost no walking and gets into narrow streets buses can't reach, but costs more (from about $69, typically $100+ per person). A walking tour is cheaper but means 10+ km on cobblestones, and a hop-on bus is cheap but stays on the big roads.
- [One day in Rome: an itinerary built around a golf cart tour](https://romegolfcartguide.com/one-day-in-rome-by-golf-cart/): To see Rome in one day, take a 3-hour golf cart tour in the morning (around 9–10am) to cover the Colosseum, Circus Maximus, the Aventine keyhole, the Pantheon, Piazza Navona, Trevi and the Spanish Steps. Have lunch in the center, then spend the afternoon inside the Colosseum or the Vatican Museums, and finish with dinner in Trastevere.
- [How to see Rome without walking](https://romegolfcartguide.com/see-rome-without-walking/): The easiest way to see Rome without walking is a golf cart tour: in about 3 hours you see 6–8 major sights, mostly from the cart, and private tours usually pick you up at your hotel. Other good options are a Vespa or vintage Fiat 500 tour with a local driver, a private car with driver, or a hop-on hop-off bus, which is cheapest but can't enter the narrow historic streets.
- [Vespa tours in Rome](https://romegolfcartguide.com/vespa-tour-rome/): Most Vespa tours in Rome are 1.5–3 hours with a professional driver: you ride as a passenger or in a sidecar, so no licence is needed. Highly rated options include the 1.5-hour Highlights Vespa Sidecar Tour with Gelato (4.9/5 from 844 reviews on GetYourGuide) and the 3-hour Sidecar Tour with Hotel Transfers & Gelato (5/5 from 268 reviews).
- [Vintage Fiat 500 tours in Rome](https://romegolfcartguide.com/fiat-500-tour-rome/): Vintage Fiat 500 tours in Rome usually last 1.5–3 hours with a local driver, and cars take 2–3 guests. The most reviewed is the City Tour in a Retro Fiat 500 with Photo Stops (4.9/5 from 952 reviews on GetYourGuide). If you want to drive yourself, there are convoy tours, which require a valid driving licence.
- [Is a golf cart tour in Rome worth it?](https://romegolfcartguide.com/is-a-golf-cart-tour-in-rome-worth-it/): A golf cart tour in Rome is worth it if you have limited time, are travelling with kids or older people, or visit in summer heat: you see 6–8 major sights in about 3 hours with almost no walking. It's less worth it if you're on a tight budget or mainly want to go inside the Colosseum or Vatican, since carts only stop outside.
- [Rome's Christmas lights by golf cart](https://romegolfcartguide.com/rome-christmas-lights-tour/): Rome's Christmas lights usually go on around 8 December and stay up until Epiphany on 6 January. A 2–3 hour evening golf cart tour can cover the lights on Via del Corso and Via dei Condotti, the trees at the Spanish Steps and Piazza del Popolo, the Christmas market in Piazza Navona, and the tree and nativity scene in St. Peter's Square.
